transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, thank you. Um, what brings me in is... I just keep getting these awful, awful doubts that I've missed something really important. Like a number on the mortgage payment, or a clause in a client proof. Actually, just last week I was doing this brochure for a local bakery—lovely people, they make these incredible sourdough loaves, though honestly, I try to stay away from gluten lately because my sister read this article about inflammation, and anyway, they wanted this specific Pantone blue for their logo. Getting the color right in print is such a nightmare compared to digital, you know? I've been a graphic designer for over thirty years, right out of college, and back then we didn't have all these... wait, what was I saying? 

Right, the doubts. So I'll check the proof, or I'll check that the front door is latched—which is a whole other thing because the wood on our porch swells in the humidity and you really have to pull it to hear it click—but even when I absolutely know I checked it, the thought just barges right back into my head. It's this loud... 'What if this is the mistake that costs you everything?' And I just can't seem to turn it off.
When these doubts come up, do you feel driven to do something over and over—like checking, counting, or repeating actions—to ease the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yes, exactly. I have to do something or the anxiety just eats at me. I end up reopening the design files, or rereading emails over and over before I can send them. And the online payment confirmations—I check those constantly. 

Actually, my bank just updated their whole web portal last month and it is just awful. They changed the main font to this incredibly thin sans-serif, maybe a light Helvetica, and it's practically illegible on a mobile screen. I don't know who they hired for their interface design, but they clearly didn't test it on anyone over forty. My husband Dave wears bifocals now, and he completely locked himself out of his account just trying to find the transfer button! It’s ridiculous. They really should have used a higher contrast ratio. 

But... wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, doing things over and over to prevent the bad things. So yeah, I check the payments, and sometimes I just have to say the figures silently in my head, repeating them until they finally feel... 'settled,' I guess? But doing all that reopening and checking means a simple invoice or a tiny logo revision turns into hours and hours of time that I just can't bill for. Which is a nightmare because freelance taxes are already so complicated, you know? My accountant was just telling me...
Can you tell me more about what happens if you don’t check or repeat those actions—does something bad actually occur, or is it more about how you feel if you don’t do them?

Well, that's the thing. Nothing bad has actually happened, at least not yet. But if I don't check, the feeling... it's just this overwhelming dread. My chest gets tight, and my stomach just drops, like I'm on a rollercoaster. Speaking of rollercoasters, Dave and I took the grandkids to that new theme park last summer, the one with the giant steel coaster? Oh my goodness, the line was two hours long, and it was so hot. I swear, the sun was just beating down on us, and they charged eight dollars for a bottle of water. Eight dollars! Can you believe that? I told Dave we should have brought those refillable bottles, you know, the insulated ones that keep ice cold for 24 hours. My niece sells them, actually. She started this little side hustle... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. The dread. If I don't check the files or repeat the numbers, I just can't shake the feeling that I've ruined everything. I know it sounds silly, because logically I know the file is fine, but the anxiety just won't let go until I do it. It's exhausting, honestly.
Do these doubts you're having feel intrusive or unwanted, like they don't really belong to you, or do they feel more like natural worries about making a mistake?

Oh, they are absolutely unwanted. It doesn't feel like a normal worry at all. Like I was saying when I first came in, it’s just these awful, awful doubts about missing something important, and they just force their way into my head. Like with the mortgage payment—which reminds me, Dave and I actually just refinanced because the rates did that little dip a few months ago, and the notary they sent to the house to sign the papers wore the most overpowering perfume. It smelled like gardenias and cheap vanilla, just completely suffocating in our small dining room. I've been so sensitive to synthetic fragrances lately, I actually had to switch all our laundry detergent to those unscented eco-friendly cardboard sheets. Which are wonderful for the environment, obviously, but they leave this strange white residue on my dark towels, and I had to run them through the rinse cycle three times just to get it out... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? The doubts, right. Do they feel natural. No, they really don't. Like I mentioned before, I'll be standing there, and I absolutely *know* I checked the client proof, or I *know* the front door is latched, but the thought just barges right back in anyway. It just invades my brain, telling me, 'What if this is the mistake that costs you everything?' It's completely unwanted. It feels like an intruder.
